brief.topic: Launching an AI feature without designing the 'I don't know' state
brief.audience: PMs and designers shipping AI assistants

coreInsight: Design the 'not sure' state before launch: say so plainly, show what was found with sources, offer a next step or a human, and track how often it happens.

hooks.text: Your AI needs a way to say “not sure.”
hooks.notes: Names a design gap teams recognise once pointed out.

hooks.text: Confidently wrong is a design bug.
The screen every AI product forgets.

caption.opening: An assistant that never says “not sure” will eventually be confidently wrong in front of a user.
body:
Design the unsure state before launch:
→ say so plainly, in one line
→ show what it did find, with sources
→ offer the next step or a human
Then track how often it happens. Rising “not sure” rates are an early signal; a rate near zero can mean it’s guessing.
